canonicalIngredients.name: pork chops (bone-in)
observations: 4 x 8 oz loin chops, 4 cm thick (s0)

canonicalIngredients.name: apples / apple sauce
observations: 6 apples, Gala or Honeycrisp, made into sauce (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: butter
observations: 1 tsp baste + 1 tbsp mounted into sauce (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: sage
observations: fresh or fried leaves, garnish, optional (s0)

canonicalIngredients.name: apple cider
observations: 1/2 cup to deglaze and loosen sauce (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: chilli (cayenne or flakes)
observations: 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes in sauce, optional (s2)

causalSequence: make apple sauce: simmer peeled chopped apples with water, sugar, vinegar 15-20 min covered; puree; stir in butter — or warm pre-made applesauce
rub chops: dijon plus salt, pepper, spice or chopped herbs
sear chops in hot ovenproof pan, 2-3 min per side, until golden
finish in 200 C oven to 63-65 C internal, 4-15 min by thickness
optional pan sauce: deglaze with cider, whisk in applesauce, mount butter off heat
serve chops with warm apple sauce; herb garnish
techniqueFacts: all three sources sear hard then finish gently; two mandate a 200 C oven finish, one makes it thick-chop-only
63-65 C (145-150 F) internal then a rest is the anti-dry lever in all three
dijon rub binds seasoning to the chop (2 sources)
sauce is always served warm; cold sauce on hot chops called a fault (1 source)
one source turns the sauce into a pan sauce: cider deglaze, applesauce whisked in, butter mounted off heat
acid balances the sauce's sweetness: cider vinegar in the sauce (1 source) or as a finishing splash (1 source tip)
bone-in chops preferred for juiciness and flavour (all three)
rub can be applied up to a day ahead and refrigerated for deeper flavour (1 source)
